Q Dark Sphere - places a sphere (0.6s delay, 6s life), effectRadius 210, spellEffects 'Aoe', attribute 'Magic Damage'; Transcendent Bonus row: 'Collecting 40 Splinters of Wrath causes Syndra to periodically stock a Dark Sphere charge, up to a maximum of 2.' R Unleashed Power - unit-targeted, targetRange 675, conjures 3 spheres and grabs up to 4 nearby live ones, attribute 'Magic Damage per Sphere'; Transcendent Bonus at 100 (execute).

SPLINTER GATES vs THE THREE SCENARIOS (identical but for the splinter count): 39 -> no gate cleared, so no second Dark Sphere charge, i.e. no Q2 cast; 60 -> 40 and 60 cleared (Q2 castable, W bonus true damage); 120 -> every gate (Q2, W true damage, E 84deg cone, R execute, P +15% AP).

RECORD DERIVED FROM THOSE ROWS:
1. cast_order is the scenario-dependent list - only the slots the splinter count can buy. Dependency edges: Q -> E (E needs a sphere on the ground to knock back, otherwise there is no stun), E -> W and E -> R (the crowd-control slot precedes the later damage slots), Q -> Q2 (Q2 is Q's recast/second charge). 39 splinters: [Q, E, W, R]; 60 and 120: [Q, Q2, E, W, R]. The passive is not a cast and takes no cast_order slot.
2. setup / consume / sources are DECLARATION-level and scenario-independent: the pre-change capture at 51db3f6 shows them byte-identical across all three scenarios, and the 39-splinter consume names Q2 - a slot 39 splinters cannot cast - which is only coherent if these lists classify the module's declared relations rather than the scenario's casts. The declared relations readable off the rows: (R1) E requires a Dark Sphere for its crowd control -> the enabler Q/Q2 is setup, E consumes; (R2) Q2 is Q's recast (the 40-splinter stocked charge) -> Q is setup, Q2 consumes; (R3) E applies crowd control -> E is setup before W; (R4) the same edge for R. So setup = {E, Q2, Q} and consume = {E, Q2}, led by the crowd-control setup relation - the relation that actually DERIVES the order and gives this scenario family its name: setup = [E, Q2, Q], consume = [E, Q2]. sources carries one line per relation, citing the declaration (cc_enabler / recast_of / cc_kind), not a damage attribute.
3. aoe maps a slot to the breadth it covers, read off the geometry fields: E carries width/angle and spellEffects 'Aoe' (the scenario's 5); P carries targeting 'Passive', affects 'Self' and null effectRadius/width/angle - a single unit, no splash - so breadth 1.

WHY THE PRE-CHANGE RECORD FAILS ON MEMBERSHIP, NOT MERELY ON ORDINALS: setup ['Q'] is a one-element list that omits E, the only crowd-control slot in the kit and the one whose stun orders the rotation; consume ['E'] omits Q2; the 39-splinter cast_order casts a Q2 that 39 splinters cannot buy; sources are hand-written damage-attribute prose ('Q Magic Damage', 'R Magic Damage per sphere') that justifies no ordering decision; aoe omits the passive. A one-element list cannot be the correct record at index 0 of a three-member set, which settles the setup[0] leaves independently of any presentation convention for the internal order.
